extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_short: examining patent citations and office actions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examiners (and related instructions for applicants/agents) on citing prior art, furnishing copies, formatting citation data, handling corrections, and ensuring completeness and clarity of Office actions during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search based on actual U.S. filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should search all applications based on the actual U.S. filing date of the application rather than on the filing date of any parent U.S. application for which priority is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the 20-year patent term and possible cancellation of priority claims, examiners should cite all material prior art having an effective filing date after the filing date of the U.S. parent application but before the actual filing date of the application being examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations included in allowed applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed applications should generally contain a citation of pertinent prior art for printing in the patent, even if no claim presented during prosecution was considered unpatentable over such prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only appropriate to send an application to issue with no art cited where a proper search has not revealed any prior art relevant to the claimed invention. If no prior art is cited, the examiner must write 'None' on form PTO-892 and insert it in the file wrapper. See MPEP § 1302.12 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling cited references in continuation applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where references have been cited during prosecution of parent applications and a continuing application (with no newly cited references) is ready for allowance, the cited references of the parent applications should be listed on a form PTO-892 and placed in the continuing application's file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In continued prosecution under 37 CFR 1.53(d) or former 1.62, it is not necessary to prepare a new PTO-892 if the form from the parent application is already in the same file wrapper and will be used by the printer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review parent applications for prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: In all continuation and continuation-in-part applications, the parent applications should be reviewed for pertinent prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must check parent files to ensure all relevant prior art is considered in the continuing prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of PCT ISR citations via IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and/or applicants' attorneys in PCT-related national applications may wish to cite the material citations from the PCT International Search Report by an information disclosure statement under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 to ensure consideration by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This advises practitioners on procedure to bring PCT-cited material to examiner attention via IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner discretion to obtain PCT ISR documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When no IDS has been filed and documents are cited in the International Search Report but neither copies nor English translations (or English family members) are provided, the examiner may exercise discretion in deciding whether to obtain the copy and/or translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may choose to take necessary steps to obtain non-English or non-provided documents cited in the ISR, but is not automatically required to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of copies of cited references
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of cited references (except as noted) are automatically furnished without charge to applicant together with the Office action in which they are cited and are placed in the application file for examiner use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of references cited by the examiner will be provided to applicant except where the documents: (B) have been referred to in applicant’s disclosure statement; (C) are cited and have been provided in a parent application; (D) are cited by a third party in a submission under 37 CFR 1.99; or (E) are U.S. Patents which are cited at allowance (see MPEP § 1302.04). See MPEP § 707.05(a) for procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-submitted citations and previously-cited references not furnished
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of references cited by applicant in accordance with MPEP § 609, § 707.05(b) and § 708.02 are not furnished to applicant with the Office action; copies of references cited in continuation applications if previously cited in the parent are not furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should check the left hand column of form PTO-892 if a copy of the reference is not to be furnished to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for preparing and furnishing copies of references
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist in providing copies of references, the examiner should write the citation on form PTO-892, place the form in the front of the file wrapper, include in the file wrapper all references to be furnished obtained from classified search files, make two copies of references located outside the classified search file (label one 'File Copy' in red ink and the other 'Applicant's Copy'), and turn the application in to technical support for counting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any application handed in without all required references will be returned to the examiner. File-handling steps, duplication, marking, and submission to technical support are specified to ensure proper furnishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design application copy provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: In design applications, procedures mirror MPEP § 707.05 (a)-(g) except that less than the entire disclosure of a cited U.S. utility patent may be supplied: copies of all sheets of drawings relied on and the first page of the specification are furnished without charge; any other subject matter relied on by the examiner will be provided without charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant desires a complete copy of a cited U.S. patent, it may be obtained through Patent and Trademark Copy Sales at usual charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant submission of prior art per MPEP §609
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP § 609 sets forth guidelines for applicants, their attorneys and agents who desire to submit prior art for consideration by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted citations will not diminish the obligation of examiners to conduct independent prior art searches or relieve examiners of citing pertinent prior art of which they may be aware. Prior art submitted in the manner provided in MPEP § 609 will not be supplied with an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of listing and pointing out features
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing references for the first time, identifying data should be placed on form PTO-892; no distinction is to be made between references on which a claim is rejected and those formerly referred to as 'pertinent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With exception of applicant-submitted citations, it is recommended that the pertinent features of references which are not used as a basis for rejection be pointed out briefly. Where applicant in an amendment refers to a reference subsequently relied upon by the examiner, such reference shall be cited using PTO-892 unless applicant listed it on a PTO-1449 or PTP/SB/08 initialed by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data required when citing U.S. patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When a U.S. patent application publication is cited by the examiner, the publication number, publication date, name of the applicant, class, and subclass should be cited on PTO-892; for U.S. patents, the patent number, patent date, name of the patentee, class and subclass should also be cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are encouraged to cite the kind codes printed on U.S. patent application publications and patents. See MPEP § 901.04 for kind codes and § 901.04/§ 901.05 for further details. Note special handling for very early X-series patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data required when citing foreign patents and applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing foreign patents, the patent number, kind code, citation date, name of the country, name of the patentee, and U.S. class and subclass, if appropriate, must be given. Foreign patents searched in TCs filing by IPC will be cited using the appropriate IPC subclass/group/subgroup and noted on PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where less than the entire disclosure is relied upon, include the sheet and page numbers specifically relied upon and the total number of sheets/pages; if entire disclosure relied on, total sheets/pages not required. See MPEP § 901.05(a) for foreign-language term chart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing non-patent literature (publications)
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing a publication, sufficient information should be given to determine the identity and facilitate location of the publication. For books, the data required by 37 CFR 1.104(d) with specific pages relied on and STIC call number will suffice; for periodicals include author(s), title, volume, issue, date, and pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the copy relied on is located only in the Technology Center, include 'Copy in Technology Center — —'. Examples of citation formats for books, parts of books, encyclopedia articles, handbooks, and periodicals are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic citation standards: no abbreviations; minimal info
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of books and periodicals SHOULD NOT be abbreviated because abbreviations may not suffice to identify the publication. Bibliographic information must be at least enough to identify the publication: author, title, and date (for books) and title, volume, date, and pages (for periodicals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These minimal citations may be made ONLY IF complete bibliographic details are unknown or unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpatent literature with document ID citation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a nonpatent literature reference with a document identification number is cited, the identification number and the class and subclass should be included on form PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format provided in text; include class/subclass and identification number to facilitate retrieval and filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain copies of external references
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original publication is located outside the Office, the examiner should immediately make or order a photocopy of at least the portion relied upon and indicate the class and subclass in which it will be filed, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office should secure copies where not locally available to preserve evidence and enable accurate citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format and retention for electronic documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO follows WIPO ST.14 recommendation; citation format for electronic documents should mirror paper-format citations with additions: (A) medium type in square brackets after title (e.g., [online]); (B) retrieval date in square brackets (four-digit year always); (C) 'Retrieved from' and the address/source; (D) specific passages indicated where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office copies of an electronic document must be retained if the same document may not be available for retrieval in the future. If an electronic document is also available in paper form it does not need to be identified as electronic unless desirable. Numerous examples provided for online databases, Internet sources, CD-ROMs, bulletin boards, e-mail, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates for declassified printed matter
rubrics_metrics.description: When using declassified material as references, consider both the printing date (preparation for limited distribution) and the publication date (date of release to public). The date of release following declassification is the effective date of publication within the meaning of the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102(a), declassified material may be prima facie evidence of prior knowledge as of its printing date even though classified at the time; such material does not constitute an absolute statutory bar and its printing date may be antedated by affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for correcting citation errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an error in citation is brought to the Office by applicant, a correction letter together with a correct copy of the reference is sent to applicant; where discovered by examiner, applicant is notified and the period for reply restarted. Examiner must correct the error in ink, initial the margin, and note the paper number of the action in which the citation is correctly given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 7.81-7.83 may be used to correct citations or copies. If an erroneous citation has not been formally corrected in an official paper in an application ready for issue, the examiner is directed to correct it by examiner's amendment accompanying the Notice of Allowability form PTOL-37. For incorrect foreign patent country citations, the General Reference Branch may assist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of decisions, orders, memoranda, and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing court decisions, give the USPQ citation and, when convenient, also the U.S., CCPA, or Federal Reporter citation; avoid citing manuscript decisions not available to the public or district court decisions reversed on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing a manuscript decision that is available to the public but unpublished, provide tribunal and complete identifying data (e.g., 'Ex parte — — , decision of the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, Patent No. — — — , paper No. — — , — — — pages.'). Decisions found only in patented files should be cited only when no published decision exists. Commissioner orders/notices not in the manual should include title and date and, where appropriate, other locating data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and clarity of examiner's action on formal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms listing informalities (PTO-948 and PTO-152) should be mailed with the examiner's first action; any additional formal requirements desired should be included in the first action. When a formal requirement is made in an examiner's action indicating allowable subject matter, the action should call attention to 37 CFR 1.111(b) and state that a complete reply must either comply with all formal requirements or specifically traverse each requirement not complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's action should be complete as to all matters, except in appropriate circumstances (misjoinder, fundamental defects), where the action may be limited to matters then before further action. Matters of form need not be raised until a claim is found allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and conduct when rejecting claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claim is refused for any reason relating to the merits, it should be 'rejected' and the ground of rejection fully and clearly stated; the word 'reject' must be used. The examiner should designate the statutory basis for any ground of rejection by express reference to a section of 35 U.S.C. in the opening sentence of each ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejected as broader than the enabling disclosure, state the reason; if rejected as indefinite, point out wherein the indefiniteness resides; if incomplete, specify lacking elements. Avoid personal language and expressions of opinion about applicant. Identify any claims judged allowable and suggest amendments to make rejected claims allowable. Avoid omnibus rejections and grouping multiple claims unless the rejection is equally applicable to all claims in the group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noting all outstanding requirements in examiner's letters
rubrics_metrics.description: When taking up an amended application for action the examiner should note in every letter all the requirements outstanding against the application; every point in the prior action still applicable must be repeated or referred to, to prevent implied waiver of the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include information under 37 CFR 1.105 and MPEP § 704.10; the examiner should determine whether such requirements have been satisfied by a negative reply under 37 CFR 1.105(a)(3). As soon as allowable subject matter is found, correction of all informalities then present should be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer all material traversed
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner must provide clear explanations of all actions taken during prosecution. Where requirements are traversed or suspension requested, make proper reference in the action on the amendment. Where applicant traverses any rejection and examiner repeats the rejection, the examiner should take note of applicant's argument and answer the substance of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant's arguments are persuasive and the previous rejection is withdrawn, the examiner must provide in the next Office communication the reasons for the withdrawal by referring specifically to the page(s) and line(s) of applicant's remarks forming the basis. It is not acceptable to merely indicate that all of applicant's remarks form the basis. Form paragraphs 7.38.01, 7.38.02, 7.37-series may be used where applicable. If a rejection of record is applied to a new/amended claim, specifically identify that ground (e.g., by citation of the paragraph in the former Office letter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of asserted advantages in applicant arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant asserts advantages (new or improved results/functions/effects) to warrant allowance, if the examiner finds the asserted advantages insufficient to overcome the rejection(s), the examiner should state the reasons for that position in the record, preferably in the action following the assertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stating reasons informs applicant and, if appealed, the Board that the asserted advantages were considered. See MPEP § 716 et seq. for affidavits/declarations (37 CFR 1.132). Form paragraphs 7.37–7.37.13 may be used where arguments are not persuasive; form paragraphs 7.38–7.38.02 where arguments are moot or persuasive.
